messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] lp in Stan's variational interface
parts: Yup. The log probability (lp) is not well-defined there for variational inference. Recall the solved parameters are parameters of the variational family, not the posterior, and the first line of the table simply takes the mean of the variational distribution, c.f., reference manual. Thus as a hack because Stan requires at least that column, we left it there while writing 0.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: lp in Stan's variational interface
parts:
On Friday, July 10, 2015 at 3:08:15 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Let's look into refactoring that into less of a hack.  We shouldn't be requiring
lp__ in anything downstream.   Feel free to bring these things up during
design, and we can look into redoing them as we go so we don't wind up with
a hack release that we want to fix later by getting rid of lp__.

Is there a lesser hack that would allow us to avoid this hack and get 2.7.0 out?

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] lp in Stan's variational interface
parts:
On Friday, July 10, 2015 at 12:19:00 PM UTC-4, Dustin Tran wrote:
Yup. The log probability (lp) is not well-defined there for variational inference. Recall the solved parameters are parameters of the variational family, not the posterior, and the first line of the table simply takes the mean of the variational distribution, c.f., reference manual. Thus as a hack because Stan requires at least that column, we left it there while writing 0.

Yes, but after it has optimized the ELBO and then draws from a multivariate normal in the unconstrained space and transforms those draws into the constrained space, can't it then evaluate the log-posterior? This seems like it would be no more or less useful than the lp__ that comes out of our MCMC algorithms. If we did that and changed the "lp" column of the csv file to "lp__", then we can worry about generalizing the csv writer until after 2.7.0.

Ben
